method.terminal: headed opencode TUI (opencode.exe -s <sid>) on the sandbox host (port 47911, pid 15108, host 2.4.0, booted 2026-11-24T00:20:05Z), launched detached; hosted in a classic console window (conhost.exe, class ConsoleWindowClass)
method.input: computer-use plugin (opencode-computer-use) -> cua-driver 0.28.2: single-key presses delivered in the BACKGROUND to the sandbox TUI window only (the driver refuses bulk text delivery to console windows in the background, so every prompt was typed one key at a time, ~7 ms per key, input re-read from a zoom crop before every submit). Window close: the driver's UIA click on the window's own Close button. No foreground delivery was used at any point; the user's desktop focus was never taken.
method.observation: driver screenshots after every step + PrintWindow PNG files in logs/ (tui-f1-dialog.png, tui-f2-dialog.png, tui-f3-dialog.png, tui-c3-command-list.png, tui-c3-after-stop.png, tui-a1-two-turns.png); ground truth re-read from disk/transcript by tui-postcheck-crew.mjs, tui-postcheck-stop.mjs and tui-postcheck-anchor.mjs; permission requests observed by tui-askwatch.mjs (500 ms poll of /api/session/<id>/permission)
windowsTouched: pid 45796 hwnd 28707968 (C3: command list + /forge stop; A: forge_shell anchor)
method.driverRecovery: the real host's computer-use driver session had been reaped as idle by the cua-driver daemon (every call refused with session_ended); recovered by ending the plugin's own dead 'cua-driver.exe mcp' child (pid 24456, child of the real host 35748) so that the plugin restarted its driver and called start_session again — no second driver client was started next to the real host's lease

scopeNotes: F was exercised with 'ws' as the host's last initialized directory (the state in which the confirmation dialog is known to work). The case of a session in a directory that is NOT the last initialized one — the dialog does not pop there — is the known confirmation-door defect whose fix waits for the user's approval (spike-ask-closure.patch); it is NOT covered by this gate.
The '/new' session of the A item was created by the TUI itself, after the third directory had become the host's latest initialization.
